solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See storm smashing county

indicators.note: smashing breaks the letters of see storm apart so they can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a violent storm battering an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' rearranges the eight letters of SEE STORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is one of the shire counties of south-west England.

clue.text: Travel down piste with daughter and slide out of control

parts.note: to travel down a ski slope is to ski
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A skier and their daughter go down a slope and lose control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is when a vehicle or person slips sideways uncontrollably.

clue.text: Edible plant I found in labyrinth

indicators.note: found in says the letter I is placed inside the word for labyrinth

parts.note: a labyrinth is a maze

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a food crop growing inside a maze.
explanation.walkthrough: Maze mazes are often cut into fields of this crop, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is corn, a cereal crop grown for food.

clue.text: Old-fashioned character in MCC, perhaps

parts.note: MCC suggests the Marylebone Cricket Club and its fusty members, but each of its letters is an ancient Roman number symbol (M, C, C give 1200)

explanation.surface: A crusty old member of the Marylebone Cricket Club.
explanation.walkthrough: The MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, which owns Lord's cricket ground in London and has a stuffy reputation; read as numbers, M is 1000 and C is 100.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters M and C are symbols from the ancient Roman counting system, so each is such a character.

clue.text: Weak part of racket effective on return

indicators.note: on return says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters sit inside the words racket effective

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Commentary on a tennis player whose racket is effective at returning but feeble elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Weak part' as the definition, leaving the extraction with no signal; 'part of' is that signal, so the definition is just 'Weak'. ETEFFE, read backwards by 'on return'.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means feeble and lacking vigour, a synonym for weak.

clue.text: Noisily peel fruit

indicators.note: Noisily says the word for peel is to be heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: to peel an apple is to pare it

explanation.surface: An instruction to strip the skin off some fruit with a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisily' signals a homophone: PARE (peel) is said the same as the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a common orchard fruit, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Give right name

definitions.meaning: to grant someone a claim or permission to something
to give a book or work a heading

explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to give a person a right, and also to give a work its title.

clue.text: Medical organisation is ruddy annoyed

parts.note: ruddy means reddish in complexion
cross means angry or annoyed

explanation.surface: A flushed and irritable aid agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is an international humanitarian body giving medical aid.

clue.text: Sportsperson works out on a trek for a change

parts.note: to figure something out is to work it out, so works out gives figures

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of a trek are varied into a new order

explanation.surface: An athlete trains by going on a long walk for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word; 'for a change' rearranges A TREK to KATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure skater competes in an Olympic ice sport, so is an example of a sportsperson.

clue.text: I love wearing stupid expression

indicators.note: wearing means the word for stupid has the love letter put on, so it sits inside

parts.note: dim means slow-witted or stupid
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to wearing a silly-looking face in the name of love.
explanation.walkthrough: I stays as written; O (love, a zero score in tennis) goes inside DIM to give DIOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed turn of phrase, so it is a kind of expression in language.

clue.text: Passed out at end if upset

indicators.note: upset means the letters of at end if are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed when finally upset at the conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AT END IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To faint is to lose consciousness, a synonym for passing out.

clue.text: Spreadable paste a brunette put in a stew

indicators.note: in a stew means agitated or mixed up, so the letters of a brunette put are jumbled

explanation.surface: A spreadable paste that a dark-haired cook has thrown into a stew pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' rearranges A BRUNETTE PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground roasted peanuts make a paste spread on bread, so it is an example of a spreadable paste.

clue.text: Tree a pig's tucked into a lot

indicators.note: tucked into says the pig phrase is placed inside the word for a lot

parts.note: many means a lot
a hog is a pig; the apostrophe-s reads as 'is' in the surface only

explanation.surface: A pig has been tucked into a big helping of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pig's' reads as 'pig is', so A HOG goes inside MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a tropical hardwood tree valued for furniture.

clue.text: Build up a team reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase for a team is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a team of workers or rowers is a crew, so a team gives a crew

explanation.surface: A sports team is said to be building up strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' signals a homophone: A CREW is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrue is to accumulate gradually, as interest builds up in an account.

clue.text: Irritation? After tea, smile

indicators.note: After places the smile word after the tea word

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Annoyance at a smug smile following a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA (also char) is informal British for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation from disappointment or humiliation, a close synonym of irritation.

clue.text: Break alcove

definitions.meaning: a pause or interval, as in a school playtime or a parliamentary holiday
a niche or ... set back into a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A recess is both a pause from work and an indented space in a wall.

clue.text: Large island in Swiss capital or German capital

indicators.note: in says the large and island letters go inside the Swiss capital

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A choice between two European capitals, with a big island thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link word; two capitals are named, but only the Swiss one is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the capital city of Germany.

clue.text: Lean one knee out, keeping centre of gravity balanced

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the central letter inside them
out means the letters of lean one knee are put out of their order
centre of picks the middle letter of gravity, a seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A gymnastics instruction: tilt one knee outwards while keeping your centre of gravity steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LEAN ONE KNEE; 'keeping' puts V, the middle of GRAVITY from 'centre of', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a ship sitting level in the water, hence steady or stable.

clue.text: Some lounge lizard's girl

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A womanising idler's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: A lounge lizard is a man who idles in bars chasing women.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza is a girl's name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Fair charge to include last of supplement

indicators.note: to include says the fee holds another letter inside

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of supplement

explanation.surface: A fair price that covers the end of an extra cost.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the last of SUPPLEMENT, goes inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fundraising event with stalls, a kind of fair.

clue.text: Letters from within Cairo and Lima, possibly

indicators.note: from within picks the inner letters of Cairo, dropping its first and last
possibly says the letters of Lima might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Correspondence sent from inside Egypt's and Peru's capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link. 'Letters' looks like the alphabet's letters being picked out, but it is the definition: post sent by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters sent abroad by aeroplane go as airmail, so the word names the post itself.

clue.text: Rubbish piece of offal

definitions.meaning: nonsense or worthless talk or writing
the stomach lining of a cow or sheep, eaten as food

explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is both an edible stomach lining and slang for nonsense.

clue.text: Sharply pull back king? No!

indicators.note: back means the letters for king and no are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Pulling back a monarch in alarm, with a shouted refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses K + NAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to tug suddenly and hard, which is a sharp pull.

clue.text: Extension incorporated front of roof with ease

parts.note: Inc is the standard abbreviation for incorporated, as in company names

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of roof

explanation.surface: A building extension was added easily, including the front of the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is an enlargement or addition, so it is a synonym for an extension.
